key_highlights: ASX 200 set to open lower following a sharp Wall Street correction led by AI and tech sell-offs.
Australian materials and mining equities demonstrate relative resilience, bolstered by regional exploration discoveries.
Domestic macro focus turns to imminent CPI data amid rising domestic recession debate and planned mid-year budget spending cuts.
AUD faces headwinds while domestic mortgage and superannuation risk profiles remain under heightened scrutiny.

sectors.trend: Severe global tech rout as AI debt burdens and high valuations trigger heavy institutional dumping.
sectors.implications: Local tech multiples will de-rate, weighing on ASX tech constituents and tech-exposed superannuation balances.

sectors.trend: Defensive rebound underway across bulk and critical minerals alongside positive exploration hits in gold, copper, and manganese.
sectors.implications: Mining majors provide index buffer against offshore tech contagion, supported by idiosyncratic drill results.

sectors.trend: Heightened scrutiny on credit buffers, asset-liability quality, and superannuation portfolio protection.
sectors.implications: Major banks face net interest margin pressure and debt serviceability scrutiny, limiting near-term multiple expansion.

sectors.trend: Persistent structural supply challenges in domestic gas and rejection of mandatory biofuel standards.
sectors.implications: Tight domestic energy market underpins upstream producer cash flows but sustains cost headwinds for commercial users.

sectors.trend: Defensive interest supported by private health insurance debate and clinical-stage oncology advancements.
sectors.implications: Provides steady capital shelter during broader cyclical downturns, though policy cross-subsidies remain contentious.

key_themes: Offshore tech valuation correction spilling into broader index sentiment
Resource sector rotation buffering ASX against severe tech-led drawdowns
Stagflationary crosscurrents ahead of domestic inflation prints and MYEFO fiscal cuts
Household debt serviceability and mortgage buffer debate impacting banking outlook

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Global Tech De-rating & Equity Market Contagion
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight high-PE growth tech equities and increase exposure to value, cash, and tangible assets.
Tilt portfolio toward non-cyclical consumer staples and essential infrastructure with defensive balance sheets.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Persistent Inflation Pressures & RBA Tightening Tail-Risk
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hold floating-rate notes and inflation-hedged resources while avoiding long-duration sovereign bonds.
Prioritize major Australian banks with top-quartile CET1 capital buffers over non-bank financial lenders.

opportunities.rationale: Miners exhibit resilient cash flows and act as an index counterbalance during global tech drawdowns.

opportunities.recommendation: Capitalise on Gold and Critical Minerals Discoveries
opportunities.rationale: High-grade exploration discoveries and boundary extensions provide strong idiosyncratic alpha.
CSL and private health insurers offer defensive earnings resilience against domestic recession risks.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge Core Equity Portfolios and Trim Beta
defensive_moves.rationale: Wall Street correction and tech plunge warrant tactical ASX 200 index put protection.

defensive_moves.recommendation: De-risk Financials Exposure Ahead of Macro Headwinds
defensive_moves.rationale: Rising serviceability stress and margin compression justify trimming premium-multiple retail banking.

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish bias over 1–3 months; ASX 200 faces volatility from Wall Street tech correction and domestic CPI prints, with materials providing the primary stabilizer.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive over 6–12 months as potential RBA easing and resources demand offset structural domestic economic deceleration.
key_catalysts: Australian monthly CPI indicator print and RBA monetary policy repricing
Federal Mid-Year Economic and Fiscal Outlook (MYEFO) spending cuts announcement
Wall Street tech sector stabilization and global interest rate trajectory
APRA review on bank mortgage serviceability buffers

Iron ore 62% Fe fines benchmark pricing and Chinese industrial demand

Australian unemployment rate and household savings drawdown rates
